newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Buoyant copper pegged to extend gains.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Buoyant copper pegged to extend gains.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30

Copper's strong advance above the key $2,440 level points to further near-term gains, with $2,490 seen as the first port of call, analysts said. Concerns about potential labour unrest in Chile are also bullish.
Aluminium, however, has been unable to penetrate tough resistance and could be due for a downside test below $1,650.
COPPER - The powerful rally on Thursday set the stage for further gains, analysts said, pegging first resistance at $2,490.

"The close of the highs is technically encouraging and is suggestive of further strength, and has on the weekly charts, confirmed an expected bullish flag pattern that had developed throughout March and April," analyst Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said in a commentary.
The pattern eventually targeted $2,600, he added.

Also underpinning the market was news that state copper workers in Chile would consider calling strike actions to protest against the government's reported plans to privatise parts of the state oil company Enap and state metals smelting firm Enami.
However, some traders sounded a note of caution about copper's immediate upside potential, noting the 14-day RSI was entering overbought territory.
"I can see copper heading up to $2,500, but its upside is probably limited beyond there. It looks overdone and it will need to consolidate," a trader said.
"It's only going to be short covering and funds buying at these levels, everyone else is going to wait until prices come back to $2,450," he added.
At 0800 GMT three months copper was quoted at $2,481/$2,485 per tonne, up $6 from the late close.
ALUMINIUM - Copper's strength showed little sign of boosting aluminium, which appeared fatigued following repeated failures to break through a tough band of resistance between $1,670 and $1,680.
Heavy forward selling on Thursday had swept aluminium off its highs and it ended the kerb at a disappointing $1,658, analysts said.
"The 10-day moving average is still providing support at $1,653 but the RSI is moving lower and the 10-day moving average shows signs of rolling over," brokers Brandeis said in a commentary.
On the downside important support was also at $1,648 and $1,634, the low from May 7.
At 0800 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,655/57 per tonne, off $2 from the late close.
--Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
